title: PDL Week 6
coldOpen:
Darren questioned Tanish's roster and got 197 dropped on him. Greg liquidated London, Jeff beat me by 53 with the Chiefs on bye, and Marv finally escaped Arizona with the catching machine he had to buy himself. 

Welcome to Week 5 of the PDL Power Rankings.

1: I don't think anyone was particularly surprised by what happened to Delco this week.

No Lamar, no Smitty, and Josh Jacobs remains on the commissioner's exempt list. Goodell could reinstate him tomorrow, and there's a decent chance I'd forget to start him because I've gotten so used to scrolling past his name.
I started Tyler Shough, who rewarded that decision with -2.16 points, and Jeff promptly beat me 160.40 to 107.34.
I actually thought my team played reasonably well considering the circumstances.
HOWEVER. I have waited a very, very long time to announce that MARVIN HARRISON JR. IS FREE.
I cannot adequately explain how excited I am that this man is finally out of Arizona.

I've defended Marv through some truly indefensible performances, convinced myself that each new week would be the one where it finally clicked, and spent the entire offseason listening to how Mike LaFleur was going to unlock him.
Remember that?
LaFleur even compared Marv to Davante Adams as a potential red-zone weapon.
New coaching staff, new offensive identity, all the training camp hype.
I ate it up.
Five weeks into the season, Marv had five receptions for 85 yards and was being traded for a second-round pick.
And the more you look into Arizona, the more you wonder how this organization is even allowed to operate.

It recently came out that Harrison reportedly requested a $50,000 Monarc Seeker, an advanced catching machine he used religiously at Ohio State that can replicate a specific quarterback's throwing motion, velocity, and trajectory.
The Cardinals declined to purchase it, so Marv eventually bought one himself.

The FOURTH OVERALL PICK asks his NFL employer for equipment to help him develop, and apparently someone in Arizona's accounting department decided that was where the franchise needed to exercise fiscal responsibility.
In retrospect, maybe they were concerned about installing a machine in the facility capable of throwing a football farther than Jacoby Brissett.
And I'm not even exaggerating how dreadful that passing offense has been.
Brissett is averaging 5.6 yards per attempt through five games, with just seven completions gaining 20 or more yards across 199 attempts.
Heading into Week 5, he had the third-lowest average depth of target in the NFL at 6.25 yards, and Arizona ranked dead last in passing explosiveness.
How exactly was LaFleur supposed to unlock Marv when the offense was apparently designed around making sure the football never traveled far enough to require a change of camera angle?
Marv has absolutely contributed to his own struggles.
The drops, inconsistent effort, and inability to establish himself ahead of Michael Wilson aren't things I'm going to pretend never happened.
I've watched the games.
Unfortunately, I've watched ALL of the games.
But he's now heading to Houston, where he'll reunite with C.J. Stroud, the quarterback who helped make him one of the most celebrated receiving prospects in college football.

For the first time since acquiring him, I have a legitimate reason to be excited that doesn't involve finding grainy footage of his 2022 Ohio State highlights and convincing myself I'm seeing something nobody else can.
Please be good, Marv. I have exhausted every other possible explanation for why this was a good decision.
2: Max scored 74.72 points this week, which is a pretty impressive way to follow up declaring last week's win over Darren his Super Bowl.
Joe lost by 43 anyway. At some point the PDL needs to investigate what having Connecticut on your schedule does to strength of record.
Max was allowed to suffer a championship hangover and still went to bed with a blowout win.
I did check to make sure Joe wasn't still leaving Kimani Vidal on his bench after last week's 10.6-point performance.
He wasn't.
Vidal actually rewarded him with 12.1 points, which unfortunately accounted for nearly 40% of Connecticut's entire offense.
Tyson Bagent was there to make sure things didn't get out of hand, completing 12 passes for 87 yards and two interceptions, finishing with -0.82 points.
Troy Hurst and Roman Wilson both contributed zero, and the entire starting WR room combined for 5.2.
You couldn't sabotage this team any more effectively if you gave Greggy access to the team.
But I also don't think Joe cares about that right now.
He's 0-5, has eight first-round picks in 2027, and has the first two picks pretty much locked up.
Jeremiah Smith had another two touchdowns against Maryland and is now sitting at 916 yards and 11 touchdowns through six games.
Nick Marsh went absolutely nuclear against Nebraska, catching six passes for 187 yards and two fourth-quarter touchdowns to rescue Indiana from an upset.

Cam Coleman finally gave Texas something to be happy about against Oklahoma, with 110 yards and a touchdown, but Arch Manning later decided being the No. 1 team in the country was getting a little exhausting and threw two fourth-quarter interceptions to help the Sooners complete the upset.
The interesting part for Joe is what happens at 1.02.
Jeremiah feels like he's already measuring the curtains in Connecticut, but the rest of this class is starting to make things a bit murky.
Jadan Baugh has cooled off considerably, Dante Moore missed another game with a concussion, and Arch is looking like he may go back for another year?
Joe desperately needs a quarterback, too.
I mean, look at that room. Bagent, McCord, Ewers, Milroe, Allar.
Tua came off the bench Sunday night, threw Atlanta's overtime possession directly to Kyle Hamilton, and Joe probably sat up and thought, "Damn, I may need to make a trade."
Fortunately, having eight firsts means he doesn't necessarily have to force a quarterback at 1.02.
He can take Smith, grab another premium prospect, and still have enough ammunition to address virtually every position on his roster.
I just want to know what happens if he walks into the draft with the first two picks, uses all eight selections, and somehow Tyson Bagent is still his starting quarterback next September.
3: I've had Week 5 circled on my calendar for months.
Kansas City was on a bye, which meant Jeff would be without Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce.
Saquon Barkley was also unavailable.
I knew this was coming before the season even started and thought there might actually be an opportunity to catch him with his pants down.
Unfortunately, Greg decided to liquidate the London Monarchs approximately 72 hours before kickoff, and Derrick Henry was suddenly in Wichita.
Terrific.
Henry immediately contributed 20.50 points, joining McCaffrey and James Cook for a combined 58.60.
Burrow and Rodgers added another 60.60 from the quarterback positions.
Jeff scored 160.40 and beat me by 53 points.
I had planned for this matchup more carefully than I've planned most major life decisions, and the result was essentially the same as if I had forgotten to set my lineup.
Remember that mailbag question about who Jeff should acquire for receiver depth since he refuses to trade for my Keenan Allen?
Darren suggested Nico Collins, I floated Khalil Shakir, and we spent a good ten minutes discussing reasonable targets.
Jeff went out and bought Derrick Henry and Courtland Sutton.
I cannot think of a more elaborate way to decline a trade offer.
The funniest part is that Sutton didn't even need to start.
Jeff absorbed a 1.50-point performance from Deebo Samuel, got next to nothing from Mark Andrews, and still comfortably exceeded the 160-point mark.
Kenneth Walker returns next week, Mahomes will be back, and Kelce is presumably returning to a tight end room that could use the help.
His backup plan for this week was Aaron Rodgers, who just threw three touchdowns against Indianapolis.
Mike outscored Jeff this week, and Tanish nearly hit 200, so I understand if there are some objections to keeping Wichita at #1.
But this was the week Jeff was supposed to be vulnerable.
I don't particularly care that he scored 17 fewer points than Mike when he managed to do all of this without three of the players who helped get him here in the first place.
There is, of course, a pretty significant price attached to the way Jeff has constructed this team.
I genuinely don't know what it would take for someone to knock Wichita off right now.
He's survived the injuries, navigated the Chiefs bye, and somehow emerged from the week with an even more ridiculous roster than the one he had seven days ago.
Is this the magical run that Wichita have been waiting for?
4: Max won this week and is being demoted.
I know he's going to have a problem with that, especially after beating Darren last week, but Hollywood just put up 142.60 against an undefeated Mike while Max managed 74.72 against Joe.
I'm not rewarding someone for drawing Connecticut on the schedule.
Now, Bryce Young was on his bye, which meant Cam Ward had to start alongside C.J. Stroud.
Funny enough, those two were actually playing against each other on Sunday.
Robert Saleh spent the week calling Houston potentially the greatest 0-4 team in the history of football, then proceeded to lose to them 26-3.
Appreciate you clearing that up, Robert.
Stroud looked good, Ward looked like Cam Ward, and Carnell Tate followed up his breakout performance with one catch for six yards.
That Tennessee stack Max has been trying to develop produced 5.1 points.
Through five games, the Titans have scored 58 points TOTAL.
I don't know how many more motivational speeches Saleh has in him before he starts threatening to put on the pads himself.
The more interesting situation is at running back.
Kyle Monangai finally broke out last week with 146 yards and two touchdowns, only to spend this week in a walking boot with turf toe.
Jordan Mason remains on IR (now on the PDL trade block), Rachaad White hasn't done much, and Woody Marks is increasingly looking like the only adult available to carry the football.
Remember that trade we discussed on the podcast?
Max sent Jalen Wright and Ollie Gordon to Mike for Caleb Douglas as part of his ongoing retool.
Well, Achane's injury has since opened the door for Gordon, who just ran for 88 yards and a touchdown against Cincinnati.
Douglas was out this week.
I still understand what Max was trying to accomplish with the trade, but watching Gordon immediately become useful while you're trying to survive with Rachaad White is some tremendous timing.
And I haven't even gotten to the receivers.
Last week Romeo Doubs and Carnell Tate helped Max knock off Darren.
This week the entire receiving group outside of Ja'Marr Chase apparently decided that victory was sufficient employment for the month of October.
McConkey is hurt again, Coker was on his bye, Worthy was unavailable, and Max is now waiting on Douglas to eventually make the trade worthwhile.
I do think there's enough here for Max to remain competitive.
Bryce is having a strong season, Stroud is improving, Chase is still Chase, and some of these younger pieces have already shown what they're capable of.
But there is a pretty significant difference between the roster that just knocked off Darren and the one we're looking at today.
Max is 3-2, ranked ninth, and currently has a worse weekly scoring average than Hollywood.
MSE being this low is just silly, and I'm giving Max free bulletin board material.
5: Well, Brett has now won two straight games.
Unfortunately for Jon, the Dragons decided to continue their little resurgence at his expense, taking Richmond down 95.44 to 44.36.

Jon's highest-scoring non-QB was Kendrick Bourne. An entire offseason spent acquiring young talent, only for a 31-year-old receiver to show up and make sure someone remembered to turn the lights on in Richmond.
I don't want to be too harsh because I still genuinely like a lot of what Jon has assembled, but his rookies are having a rough introduction to the NFL.
I know we had a recent mailbag giving him some sunshine, but the power rankings will snap him back to reality.
Sadiq followed up last week's goose egg by fumbling against Cleveland and subsequently leaving with a concussion.
Lemon is at least starting to look involved in Philadelphia's offense, but consistently gets outplayed by other passcatchers.

I've also realized Jon has managed to tie a significant portion of his rebuild to the New York football market. Sadiq is on the Jets, Fields is on the Giants, and Antonio Williams is across the field in Washington.
The Giants and Commanders just played 70 minutes of football and somehow BOTH left without a win, while the Jets needed everything they had to beat Cleveland 17-12.
I don't know if we can get Jon some sort of federal assistance here, but investing your franchise's future into these three organizations feels like it should qualify you for something.
There was at least some Fernando Mendoza action this week!
Granted, it took New England beating the absolute shit out of Vegas for him to finally see the field, but he completed six of eight passes in relief of Kirk Cousins.
Darren spent a good portion of the latest podcast predicting Mendoza would eventually replace Kirk, potentially after the bye.
If the Raiders keep playing like they did against New England, Jon might get to see his rookie quarterback a whole lot sooner than anticipated.

Jon inherited a terrible situation, went heavy into a rookie class he believed in, and now has to sit through the part of a rebuild where everyone is either injured, buried on a depth chart, or employed by the New York Jets.
Jesus Christ, Kendrick Bourne might actually be the veteran leadership this team needs.
6: I feel like I am part of the college committee again because I am attributing this week's great loss in quality to the juggernaut known as the Southern Oregon Smoke.
Brian scored 142.60 points this week and lost by nearly 35.
Mike is now 5-0 after dropping 177.36 on him, which is normally where I'd just tell Brian he had some rough luck and move along.
Except I went through his bench and found something that I really wish I hadn't.
MarShawn Lloyd over Jeremiyah Love.
Kyle Williams over Tee Higgins.
Pat Freiermuth over Brenton Strange.
Those three changes would have given Brian 177.70 points.
He could have handed Mike his first loss of the season by 0.34.
Instead, he got rocked. I'm sure Brian will appreciate me bringing this to everyone's attention.
Now, I'm not going to pretend any reasonable person was benching the 1.01 Jeremiyah Love for MarShawn Lloyd before kickoff, but holy shit is Arizona becoming frustrating (MARV IS FREE!).
Mike LaFleur spent September reminding everyone that it's a "looong season" and apparently 12 carries for 22 yards is about all the work he's comfortable giving the kid.
Brian has two Loves on his roster.

One threw for 367 yards against Chicago, and the other is getting the NBA load-management treatment five weeks into his professional career (Greggy is no longer gonna continue reading because I made a basketball reference).
Meanwhile, Parker Washington spent Sunday morning ruining my life in London.
Egbuka is producing, Tuten has been getting work, and Braelon Allen just had his best game of the season.
Even with Nico coming back down to earth after last week's explosion, Hollywood still put up one of the better scores in the league.
He said he wanted to bring some chaos, and boy, Hollywood is having a different type of energy now.
Which brings me back to the podcast.
Darren was once again advocating for Brian to sell Nico Collins, along with potentially moving Cousins and Freiermuth.
I'm not so sure.
He's 1-4 with a roster that just demonstrated it has enough scoring potential to beat Mike.
Of course, the problem with that argument is that we've now spent five weeks talking about all the things Brian COULD be doing while he continues to lose actual football games.
And now Houston has agreed to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., meaning Nico is about to share a receiving room with the guy I traded Derrick Henry to acquire.
Great.
My own questionable investment decisions have somehow found a way to interfere with Brian's roster without either of us making a trade.
I'm actually starting to get a little concerned about Hollywood.
He's got considerably more depth than expected, three functioning fantasy quarterbacks, and enough tight ends to start his own AFC South.
The record looks awful, but he doesn't own his 2027 first, so there's no real incentive to deliberately bottom out either.
As the man holding that pick, I'm going to pretend I never did the 177.70 calculation.
7: I'd like to formally withdraw my participation in last week's Tanish slander.

Darren and I spent an unreasonable amount of time on the podcast questioning why the defending champion, who desperately needs wide receiver depth, decided to trade for Jameis Winston and Seth McGowan instead.
His receiving room is one Rashee Rice injury away from starting Mack Hollins, and his solution was to acquire a fourth quarterback and ANOTHER running back.
Darren couldn't understand it.
I couldn't understand it.
Perfectly reasonable criticism from two experienced PDL owners who apparently know absolutely nothing about football.
Tanish responded by scoring 197.70 points against Darren.
I think we should have him back on the podcast to discuss his next trade.
Maybe he can get a fifth quarterback.
And what an absolutely miserable way for Darren to lose.
Stafford throws for 383 yards and three touchdowns, Gibbs puts up 35.20, Bowers delivers another 23, and the Thunder finish with 174.82 points.

That would've been enough to comfortably beat nearly everyone else this week. Instead, Darren gets to experience the same helplessness he routinely inflicts on the rest of the league, which I'm sure has absolutely devastated the PDL community.
The particularly painful part is that Philadelphia could've won this game.
CeeDee Lamb contributed 1.90 points while Mike Evans sat on the bench with 22.80.
Making that substitution alone would've brought Darren to 195.72, STILL short of Tanish.
However, had he also started Deshaun Watson over Sam Darnold, Philadelphia would've finished with 201.62 and walked away victorious.
Remember Darren's latest podcast take about how he's still not buying the Deshaun Watson resurgence?
Well, Watson has now outscored at least one of his starting quarterbacks in every single week of the season, and Darren continues to treat him like he's waiting for the results of a second opinion.
At this point, Watson could win Comeback Player of the Year and Darren would still want to see how he performs in next year's preseason.
It's a frustrating loss because I genuinely think Philadelphia remains one of the most complete teams in the league.
Gibbs is currently RB1, Bowers is producing like the best tight end in football, and Stafford has been terrific.
Even with Lamb disappearing Thursday night, the Thunder put up one of the highest scores of the season.
Very few teams have that kind of margin for error.
I do have one request, though.
Darren, could you spend the next podcast explaining everything wrong with my roster?
Maybe tell everyone how poorly I've managed my running backs, question why I traded for Marv, and really dig into the quarterback situation.
Whatever you said to Tanish appears to be working.
8: Dak Prescott threw for 316 yards Thursday night.
I'm putting that first because someone looking at the box score six months from now might be under the impression he played a decent football game.
He did not.

Dallas lost AT HOME to an 0-4 Tampa Bay team starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, Dak threw two interceptions, including one that effectively ended their comeback attempt, and the Cowboys somehow managed to make Todd Bowles look like he had everything under control for three consecutive hours.
It was an incredible hate watch.
And the entertainment didn't stop there!
As Dak was heading to the locker room, a third-party car-service driver called the performance "embarrassing," which apparently upset Dak enough to get security involved.
My favorite part is that the one person at AT&T Stadium willing to give Prescott an accurate performance review didn't even work for the Cowboys.
Unfortunately for Welch, that was his starting quarterback.
And despite all of that, Welch scored 162.28 points and comfortably dispatched Greg, who was apparently too busy holding an estate sale to prepare for their matchup.
I'm becoming increasingly impressed with this roster.
Jared Goff is having a terrific season, Christian Watson has become a legitimate weekly difference-maker, and McBride continues to smash.
Hell, even the bench showed out this week. Demario Douglas scored 20.50, Cooper had 14.10, and Jacoby Brissett put up 29.78.
Yes, the same Jacoby Brissett I just spent the Delco write-up criticizing.
Had Welch started Brissett over Dak, he would have finished with 179.42 points, outscoring BOTH undefeated teams this week.
Please don't let Dak see those numbers.
He's going to have the shuttle driver escorted out of Welch's house, too.
Welch has finished second in the PDL twice.
Twice!
I think this could be one of his better opportunities to finally win the whole thing.
There's enough firepower here to compete with Mike and Jeff, especially with how well Watson and Goff are playing.
The receiving depth is excellent, he's loaded at quarterback, and Bucky just reminded everyone why he was such a valuable dynasty asset in the first place.

I'm still concerned about the running backs behind him, though. Montgomery contributed 1.1 points this week, Benson and Conner remain on IR, and the position gets considerably less exciting once you get past Irving.
Remember last week when Derrick Henry hit the block, and Darren identified Welch as a potential buyer?
Well, Henry is now in Wichita, along with Courtland Sutton. Jeff is undefeated and apparently has no intention of leaving any veteran talent available for the rest of us.
Welch has a legitimate championship window here, but he might need one more move to keep pace with those two at the top.
If he finishes second for a third time, I know a shuttle driver in Arlington who can handle the postgame interview.
9: Well, Greg actually did it.
During the latest podcast, Darren was asked whether London was really selling and spent several minutes explaining that outside of Derrick Henry, there weren't many obvious pieces for Greg to move.
Apparently, somewhere in the two weeks Greg has been missing from the show, he's developed the ability to hear us talking shit remotely.
In less than 24 hours, Henry, Tee Higgins and Courtland Sutton were all gone.
I genuinely expected to wake up Sunday morning to find Bijan Robinson on the block and Greg asking if anyone needed a lightly used Hunter Henry.
Henry went to Jeff for his 2028 first and a 2029 second.
Higgins went to Brian for Jayden Noel and Brian's 2028 first, and Sutton was subsequently shipped to Jeff for a third.
Remember, Greg only JUST acquired Sutton as part of the Chris Olave trade with Mike.

He spent two years trying to acquire Rome Odunze, finally got his guy, and somehow that transaction has now resulted in him supplying Mike with Olave and Jeff with Sutton. Oh, and Jeff also has Derrick Henry now.
There doesn't appear to be a formal alliance between the league's two undefeated powerhouses, but Greg has been kind enough to personally supply both of them.
I picked this man to win the championship, and he's currently doing more to improve Mike and Jeff's chances of winning it than either of their own scouting departments.
The actual football wasn't much better. Welch absolutely dismantled London 162.28 to 90.46, with Nix and Herbert combining for just over 21 points.
Odunze, the man Greg reportedly needed 46 offers to acquire, finished with 3.5 and a fumble.
Meanwhile, Jayden Noel, who arrived in the Higgins trade approximately five minutes ago, caught one pass for 54 yards and a touchdown.
One catch was worth almost four times Rome's entire afternoon.
I'm sure Greg is handling that tremendously well.
Getting two additional 2028 firsts, especially one belonging to an aging Wichita roster that's already spent a small country's GDP trying to win this season, could pay off handsomely.
Bijan and Judkins aren't going anywhere, and there's still a reasonable young foundation here.
My issue is more with the speed at which this whole thing happened.
Five weeks ago, London was one of the teams I thought could win the PDL.
Last week he was still putting up 140 points against Jeff.
Now I'm looking at a starting lineup featuring Devaughn Vele, Jayden Noel and Emanuel Wilson, wondering if I've accidentally opened his 2023 roster.
Oh, and Darren predicted on the podcast that if Greg traded Henry, Delco would probably have the inside track on the sixth playoff seed.
Greg, buddy, you didn't have to do all this for me. I appreciate it, though.
10: The Giants and Commanders played 70 minutes of football Sunday and finished in a 27-27 tie.
Mike somehow won the game.
Isaiah Likely caught 11 passes for 94 yards and two touchdowns, finishing with 32.40 points while the two actual NFL teams involved couldn't figure out how to beat each other.
It's a remarkable achievement to play an entire overtime period and have the only winner be some guy in Oregon checking Sleeper.
And poor Brian.
Hollywood finally put together a genuinely impressive week, scoring 142.60 points, only to get 177.36 dropped on his head.
I can only imagine Mike's anxiety watching Monday night's Bills-Rams shootout, where Josh Allen and Puka Nacua were playing against one another and Mike was somehow rooting for both.
They combined for 60.70 points.
I don't even think this was a particularly clean performance from Southern Oregon.
Olave had a quiet afternoon, Waddle contributed 3.80 points, and TreVeyon Henderson managed four carries before leaving with another injury.
Mike has Achane on IR, Charbonnet on PUP, and is now relying on the Miami backfield he acquired from Max to keep things moving.
Fortunately, Ollie Gordon delivered 88 rushing yards and a touchdown against Cincinnati.
The Dolphins lost, naturally, but at least someone benefited from the transaction.
Meanwhile, George Pickens had 130 yards and a touchdown sitting on Mike's bench.
Puka is back to putting up WR1 numbers, Jefferson scored again, and LaPorta has been producing like the player we thought we'd see last season.
I'm also becoming increasingly concerned about what happens when Achane eventually returns, assuming Miami hasn't placed its entire offensive roster on injured reserve by then.
I realize the optics of keeping Mike at #2 after a 177-point performance are going to be difficult to defend, particularly when Jeff scored 160.40 this week.
Both are 5-0, Jeff still has the season-long scoring advantage, and the Whirlwind just acquired Derrick Henry AND Courtland Sutton.
I don't think there's a more appropriate time to preserve the status quo, although I'm sure Mike will find something objectionable about that sentence.
What makes Southern Oregon particularly dangerous is that there really isn't much left to address outside of the running back situation.
He's got two elite quarterbacks, arguably the best receiving room in the PDL, and two tight ends who combined for 52.20 points this week.
The fact that Brian scored 142 and never really had a chance is pretty terrifying.
Jeff just spent a 2028 first, a second, and a third to acquire Henry and Sutton.
Apparently, that's what it costs to keep Mike in second place.
11: Brett has now won two straight games, this time without Tetairoa McMillan, who was on his bye after single-handedly resurrecting Dubrovnik last week.

Granted, the opponent was Jon, who scored 44.36 points, so we're not exactly booking flights to a championship parade. But there are some things happening here that I think deserve a little more attention.
That's his third touchdown of the season, putting him at WR17 through five weeks while playing for a Cleveland offense that just managed to lose 17-12 to the Jets.

I still can't get over how quickly Boston has established himself, especially considering how much of the preseason discussion around Cleveland's rookies revolved around Kevin Concepcion (I did that for you, Darren).
Boston currently has more fantasy points than Tetairoa McMillan (with an extra game played).
Brett might actually have something pretty special brewing between those two.
Which makes the podcast discussion about Carnell Tate even more painful.
Darren was asked whether Greg trading Olave to Mike was approaching the territory of Brett's Tate trade, and somehow concluded that Brett's was STILL worse.
For those who need a reminder, Brett drafted Tate at 1.04 and subsequently traded him for what is looking increasingly like the 1.12 in next year's draft.
The man could have had McMillan, Boston AND Tate together.
Instead, he's going to spend the next six months watching Indiana highlights and convincing himself Charlie Becker is the missing piece.
Also, Brian Robinson deserves a shoutout.
Last week Brett left his 25.2 points on the bench.
This week he finally promoted him to the starting lineup, where he promptly received one carry for seven yards and finished with 1.6 points.
Dobbins, meanwhile, put up another respectable performance and remains on the trade block.

With Hampton's workload becoming increasingly frustrating and Dart still on IR, I'd still like to see Brett capitalize on the veteran pieces he has rather than get distracted by two wins over Brian and Jon.
There's an actual young foundation here, even if the trade history is going to require a little creative finesse.
12: Tanish currently has four quarterbacks on his roster.
Three of them scored at least 31.74 points this week, and Caleb Williams didn't even play.
I've spent the better part of a month questioning his roster construction, but I'm starting to consider the possibility that Tanish has figured out something the rest of us haven't.
I don't particularly like where this is heading.
197.72 points against Darren.
Nearly TWO HUNDRED.

I would have loved to see Darren's face when he checked the matchup after getting 33 from Stafford, 35 from Gibbs and another 23 from Bowers, only to discover that he was still getting absolutely handled by the team whose offseason strategy we've spent half the podcast trying to understand.
Drake Maye was responsible for most of the early damage, throwing four touchdowns and running in another against Vegas.
He finished with 47.46 points, the highest quarterback score of the season so far.
Jaylen Warren then decided that Pittsburgh's entire offense should run through him, producing 188 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, including an 80-yard reception.
Meanwhile, Nabers is really looking like Nabers again, catching 11 passes for 121 yards and a touchdown.
But I need to revisit the Jameis Winston trade because something genuinely ridiculous happened Sunday.
Tanish started Jayden Daniels against the Giants, who finished with 32.26 points.
On the OTHER sideline was his newly acquired Jameis Winston, who rallied New York from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit and scored another 31.74 from Tanish's bench.
He managed to extract 64 combined fantasy points from both starting quarterbacks in a game where neither NFL team could figure out how to win.
The most concerning part for the rest of us is that this wasn't even an especially complete performance from Boulder.
Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown combined for 15.2 points, Dalton Kincaid contributed 3.7, and Cody White was once again occupying that third receiver spot we've been begging Tanish to address.
Those four starters combined for 24.3 points, and the Bears STILL nearly cracked 200.
I do think that receiving depth remains a legitimate concern, especially with Rashee Rice dealing with a hamstring injury.
JSN has been outstanding, Nabers is starting to look healthy, and the running back collection is as excessive as ever.
If Tanish actually adds another dependable receiver, there's very little separating this roster from the two undefeated teams above him.
Then again, he's the defending champion, he's 4-1, and he just beat one of the best teams in the league with Jameis Winston putting up 31.74 points on his bench.
Maybe the rest of us should be taking notes.
